Main Input: H&E histology images plus method training evidence from spatial transcriptomics
Main Use in This Topic: predict spatial gene expression at single-cell resolution from histology
Key Difference: Targets single-cell-resolution expression from histology and uses subcellular spatial-transcriptomics evidence, whereas most earlier histology routes are spot-level or broader multimodal foundation models.
Evidence Note: Direct PubMed evidence verifies PMID 40954301 and DOI 10.1038/s41592-025-02795-z; the frozen Layer 1 input provides the GitHub link. Resolution and comparator cues are Layer 2 synthesis from the method abstract and topic context.
Best First Choice When: When the stated goal is histology-driven gene-expression prediction with single-cell-resolution output as the central selection cue.
Do Not Start With This When: When only spot-level prediction is needed, no histology is available, or low-resource CPU-first screening is the first constraint.
Prediction-risk Caveat: Single-cell-resolution prediction from histology is vulnerable to training-domain shift and resolution-inflation risk if not validated against measured spatial data.

Main Input: H&E image patches plus spatial coordinates around measured spots
Main Use in This Topic: predict spot-level spatial transcriptomics from histology
Key Difference: Combines image-patch features, Transformer spatial context, and graph-neural-neighbor structure for histology-to-expression prediction.
Evidence Note: Direct PubMed evidence verifies PMID 35849101 and DOI 10.1093/bib/bbac297; the frozen Layer 1 input provides the GitHub link. Alternative and scale cues are Layer 2 synthesis.
Best First Choice When: When histology-to-spot-expression prediction is the target and a transformer-plus-graph route is appropriate to read first.
Do Not Start With This When: When the task is reference-assisted missing-gene imputation, uncertainty calibration of existing predictions, or single-cell reconstruction.
Prediction-risk Caveat: Method-paper benchmarking does not remove cross-cohort, tissue, staining, and scanner domain-shift risk.

Main Input: spatial expression matrix plus matched or relevant scRNA-seq reference
Main Use in This Topic: enhance spatial expression by predicting genes from a shared latent space with scRNA-seq
Main Output: spatial whole-transcriptome enhancement / predicted gene expression
Key Difference: Uses shared latent-space alignment for scRNA-assisted enhancement rather than histology-image prediction or deep generative cellular reconstruction.
Evidence Note: Direct PubMed evidence verifies PMID 32955565 and DOI 10.1093/nar/gkaa740 and reports whole-transcriptome prediction using scRNA-seq; the frozen Layer 1 input provides the GitHub link. Comparator and resource labels are Layer 2 synthesis.
Best First Choice When: When a suitable scRNA-seq reference exists and the goal is transcriptome-wide enhancement of measured spatial locations.
Do Not Start With This When: When no tissue-relevant scRNA-seq reference exists or the intended route must be histology-only.
Prediction-risk Caveat: Reference mismatch, batch effects, and missing cell states can be transferred into predicted spatial expression.

Best First Choice When: When the selection branch needs cellular-resolution reconstruction by integrating spatial and single-cell transcriptomics.
Do Not Start With This When: When the task is simple spot-level histology prediction or when a suitable single-cell reference is unavailable.
Prediction-risk Caveat: Deep generative reconstruction can mix reference bias with apparent high-resolution detail; downstream biological validation is essential.

Do Not Start With This When: When low-resource CPU-first analysis is required or pretrained image-prior effects should be avoided.

Main Input: single-cell spatial transcriptomics plus scRNA-seq reference
Main Use in This Topic: impute missing genes in single-cell spatial transcriptomics with coupled cell-type annotation
Key Difference: Targets single-cell spatial missing-gene imputation and annotation jointly, using supervised latent-space guidance from scRNA-seq.
Evidence Note: Direct PubMed evidence verifies PMID 40057378 and DOI 10.1093/nar/gkaf158. Annotation coupling is direct evidence; resource, scale, and comparator cues are Layer 2 synthesis.

Do Not Start With This When: When annotation should remain separate from imputation or no suitable scRNA-seq reference is available.
Prediction-risk Caveat: Joint imputation and annotation can create circular support between predicted genes and predicted labels.
